newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends up vs dlr despite RBI, looks firm.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends up vs dlr despite RBI, looks firm.

text.p: The Indian rupee edged firmer against the dollar on Monday in both the forward and spot markets despite central bank intervention, dealers said.
The rupee ended at 35.79/80 against the weekend close of 35.805/815. The rupee opened Monday at 35.795/805.
Dealers said Reserve Bank of India (RBI) dollar purchases briefly pushed the rupee down to the day's low of 35.805 but the rupee rallied to its closing level on strong supply of dollars.
They said most of Monday's trade was between 35.795 and 35.80, with stray deals at 35.79.
"Dollar supply was strong today," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "Further, RBI buying was on a low scale."
Dealers estimated the RBI dollar purchases at $30-40 million and said it was not enough to weaken the rupee substantially.
They said the rupee was likely to move up further and test the 35.75 per dollar mark later this week unless the RBI bought dollars in a big way.
Dealers said the cental bank bought dollars in both the spot and forward markets on Monday.
"In spot, they bought between 35.795 and up to 35.805," said another dealer. "In forwards they bought outright June and July delivery dollars."
The impact on forward premiums was marginal as the RBI purchases were not big and market sentiment on the forward rupee remained bullish, he said.

"Domestic liquidity is showing signs of easing," he said. "Call money rates have been coming down steadily through last week and fell below 7.0 percent today after being stuck around 8.0 percent for most of last week," he said. "Premiums will remain easy on improved sentiment."
The annualised premium for six-month dollars ended Monday at 4.58 percent against the weekend close of 4.64 percent, dealers said.
